transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Lynx CTO), Ravi Kapoor (Lynx Head Eng), Sam Lee (Lynx Security)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining for the data retention and PII controls walkthrough, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'll kick things off and Priya will demo the console and API examples.
[00:18] Maya: Hi Alex, thanks. We specifically want to understand how Redwood handles request storage and redaction, because we can't have raw cardholder data leaving our environment.
[00:28] Alex: Totally, that's the core of today's, um, demo. We'll cover the store_requests API flag, the console toggles to disable request storage per-organization or per-route, how logging redaction works, and how KMS integrates for at-rest encryption.
[00:43] Ravi: Quick perf question up front — if we turn off request storage, does that prevent metrics or tracing that we rely on?
[00:53] Priya: Good question. Short answer: turning off store_requests stops full request bodies from being persisted. We still emit anonymized metrics and token-level telemetry for billing and latency SLOs, but we can avoid storing prompt/response text. There's also an option to enable prefix/KV cache while keeping storage disabled in some configurations — we can show the tradeoffs.
[01:15] Sam: And for auditability — we need immutable audit logs for who accessed what and when, even if the payload is redacted.
[01:22] Alex: Yes, audit logs are separate. We keep access events in audit trails (user, API key, route, timestamp). The actual request payloads can be redacted or never stored depending on the store_requests toggle. Audit logs themselves are retention-configurable and can be shipped to your SIEM via S3 or Syslog.
[01:38] Maya: Our PCI team will ask about encryption keys — do you integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[01:44] Priya: We support provider KMS integrations — AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer-managed HSMs for private deployments. For hosted we can use CMKs in your account (cross-account with grant) so you control key rotation and revocation.
[01:58] Alex: For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers put keys behind their KMS/HSM and Redwood stores only ciphertext. We also provide key identifiers in audit logs so you can prove key usage.
[02:10] Maya: Makes sense. Walk us through the console — show the retention toggles and where the redact options live.
[02:16] Priya: Sure, I'm sharing my screen now. (screen share noise) Ok, this is the Redwood Console, on the left nav there's Privacy & Retention settings. At the org level you can set default request retention to 0 days, 7, 30, 90, or custom.
[02:33] Priya: Here is a per-route override — for our payments route you can flip 'Store requests' to off. We also have a 'Redact detected PII' checkbox which leverages built-in PII heuristics (credit card regexes, SSN patterns, names/emails heuristics).
[02:50] Ravi: Is that PII detection deterministic, or ML-based fuzzy detection? We need low false positives.
[02:57] Priya: It's hybrid — regex-based for structured items like PANs and SSNs, and a lightweight ML model for contextual PII (names, addresses). You can tune sensitivity or provide your own patterns. There's also an allowlist/denylist for tokens you want to preserve.
[03:12] Sam: If the model redacts something incorrectly, can we request a raw view for debugging?
[03:18] Priya: Yes, but that raw view is gated by RBAC and is itself logged in the audit trail. For hosted customers you can also enable time-limited debug snapshots that expire and can be auto-purged.
[03:30] Alex: Another important part is the API flag. If you're calling the Redwood API programmatically you can set store_requests=false and redact_logs=high or redact_logs=auto depending on your needs.
[03:40] Alex: Example: POST /v1/generate with {"model": "redwood-1", "prompt": "...", "store_requests": false, "redact_logs": "auto"} — that will avoid persisting the prompt/response while still returning the model output synchronously.
[03:55] Maya: Wait — if store_requests is false, can we still use debug endpoints for a given request id later?
[04:02] Priya: No, if store_requests is false at ingestion the payload is not persisted so there's no later retrieval of that raw exchange. We expose a transient request_id in logs for tracing, but the text is absent. For debugging you can set store_requests to true for a test route or enable session recording for a short time window.
[04:18] Ravi: How do you handle embeddings or vector stores where we might unintentionally store PHI?
[04:24] Priya: Good point. Embeddings are stored only if explicitly enabled; there's a separate toggle for embeddings persistence and you can set retention windows. Additionally, we support automatic hashing of embedding inputs, and you can opt to store only metadata (no vector values). For customers doing vector search with PHI, we recommend a private deployment and bring-your-own-encryption model.
[04:45] Maya: Can you demonstrate how the audit logs look when a redaction happens?
[04:50] Priya: Sure — switching windows. Here's an audit line: {event: "request.received", user: "svc-lynx-ingest", route: "/payments/authorize", request_id: "r_12345", stored: false, pii_redacted: ["card_number"], key_id: "arn:aws:kms:..."} — you'll see redaction reasons and which patterns matched. (note: transcription may show curly braces, sometimes flattened)
[05:12] Sam: Ok, good to have the key_id. For compliance we need exportable audit reports for a date range.
[05:18] Alex: You can export audit logs to S3 with lifecycle rules; we also support a CSV export from Console for ad-hoc reporting.
[05:25] Maya: What about SSO and RBAC? We have fine-grained roles in our org.
[05:30] Priya: Redwood supports SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls. Admins can limit who can toggle retention or view raw logs; you can also set a separate 'security-only' role that gets audit-read but not payload access.
[05:46] Ravi: Any limitations if we go with Dedicated vs Hosted? For latency and cost.
[05:52] Alex: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and you can control key ownership and VPC. Hosted is faster to onboard, but for strict PCI or data residency you should look at Dedicated or Private deployment. We'll include pricing and commit options in follow-up.
[06:08] Maya: For Private deployment, does Redwood still manage any control plane components?
[06:12] Priya: For VPC-hosted Private deployments we've a customer-controlled control plane option: you run the control plane in your account and Redwood provides the operator manifests. For fully air-gapped, we provide an on-prem bundle and you operate the entire stack.
[06:26] Sam: On the topic of redaction accuracy — can we bring a sample dataset for a POC so you can tune the heuristics?
[06:32] Priya: Absolutely. For pilots we sign an NDA and then you can upload sample logs to the test tenant. Priya: We'll run evaluation scripts that show precision/recall for detected PII and iterate on patterns.
[06:45] Alex: Let's pivot to a live API demo — Priya, you want to run a quick curl?
[06:49] Priya: Yep. (typing) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lynx-demo" -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"charge customer card 4242-4242-4242-4242 for $12.50","store_requests":false,"redact_logs":"auto"}'
[07:10] Priya: Response returns output but in the backend the prompt is not stored. I can show the request in the request inspector — here you see request_id r_78a, stored: false, pii_redacted: ["card_number"].
[07:22] Ravi: I see. If we run thousands of requests, can we key-by-customer and keep only a hashed pointer?
[07:29] Priya: Yes, we support hashing with a HMAC using your key so you can correlate events without storing raw data. That way you keep the pointer in logs but not the content.
[07:38] Maya: For RLHF or quality evals, sometimes we need full transcripts. Can we route a small percentage of traffic to a persisted route?
[07:44] Alex: You can do sampling — route 1% to store_requests=true for evaluation, or use Canary rollouts at the route level. Console has traffic split controls so you can do A/B with different retention policies.
[07:58] Priya: Also to note: Redwood Optimize recommends batching/quantization settings, but these do not affect retention controls — they're orthogonal.
[08:06] Sam: How are redaction patterns updated? Is there a changelog?
[08:10] Priya: Yes, pattern changes are versioned and you can opt into automatic updates or vet them in a staging tenant. Changes that affect redaction decisions produce a changelog and a preview mode.
[08:22] Maya: Can Redwood provide a SOC2 attestation and penetration test results?
[08:26] Alex: We'll share the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. We also publish our recent pentest summary and third-party security assessments.
[08:35] Ravi: Ok nice. Let's talk about retention windows — are there hard limits?
[08:39] Priya: For hosted customers, retention is configurable up to a year via the Console. For Dedicated you can set custom retention beyond that and integrate with your own archival. For on-prem you control retention entirely.
[08:52] Maya: Can we automate purge policies so data older than X days is removed and cannot be recovered? We have to certify secure deletion.
[08:58] Priya: Yes, purge policies are irreversible once executed in the hosted control plane. For extra assurance, when you use customer KMS keys and rotate them, you can revoke keys to make ciphertext effectively unrecoverable (we'll show the key lifecycle doc).
[09:14] Sam: One more deep question: embeddings — you mentioned option to hash. If a vector store still exists and someone queries it, could the original text be reconstructed?
[09:23] Priya: Reconstruction is extremely unlikely from hashed or one-way transformed vectors; however, as a best practice we recommend not storing embeddings of sensitive PHI in shared hosted environments. Private deployments with BYOK are recommended for high-risk data.
[09:36] Maya: This looks promising. Can we see what the console audit export looks like?
[09:40] Priya: Switching to audit export page — you can select dates, filters by route/user, and export to CSV or S3. The CSV columns include event_time, user, route, request_id, stored_flag, pii_redaction_list, key_id.
[09:54] Ravi: Do you capture raw IP addresses in logs? We have an IP minimization policy.
[09:59] Alex: We capture source IPs for security but you can request IP anonymization where we store only /24s or hash the IP. That's a per-customer toggle.
[10:08] Sam: For the pilot, our security team will want a hands-on checklist and a runbook for incidents. Can Redwood share a runbook template?
[10:14] Alex: Yes, we'll include our incident response runbook and a playbook for data-exposure scenarios.
[10:20] Maya: Great. Any questions on your side, Priya?
[10:24] Priya: Not yet — I'll walk through a few edge cases. For example, long prompts: we have truncation + redaction order — PII detection runs before any retention policy to make sure redaction is applied at ingestion even if a request is later truncated for cost reasons.
[10:40] Ravi: What about compliance for EU customers — data residency?
[10:45] Priya: We support region-restricted retention and data locality. For EU-only data you can pin to EU regions and prevent cross-region replication. For Dedicated we can deploy in your preferred cloud region.
[10:58] Maya: Let's cover a sample timeline — what does a pilot look like?
[11:02] Alex: Typical pilot: 1) sign NDA, 2) provision test tenant in hosted or dedicated, 3) run ingestion with sample data 1-2 weeks, 4) evaluate PII redaction precision, 5) run perf benchmarks (latency, KV cache), 6) security review and contract. We usually aim for 4-6 weeks.
[11:21] Priya: I'll outline specific benchmark metrics: p95 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, and storage costs with and without request retention.
[11:31] Maya: For billing we need to know cost delta when enabling request storage for 1% sampling.
[11:36] Alex: We'll provide an estimated bill impact sheet showing storage cost per GB and approximate per-request overhead.
[11:42] Ravi: Can the console show cost by route so we can see which endpoints are driving storage?
[11:46] Priya: Yes — cost breakdown by route and token is available in Redwood Console's billing view.
[11:52] Sam: Any gotchas for logging in containerized environments — we use sidecars to call the API — anything to watch for?
[11:58] Priya: Make sure you don't log raw prompts in your application logs; we recommend client-side redaction prior to sending when possible, and to use store_requests=false from client-side. We can provide a library snippet for common languages to mask tokens or PII before transmitting.
[12:14] Maya: Ok, let's jump back to the live console to show the step-by-step toggle change and then simulate a request.
[12:19] Priya: (screen) Going to Routes > payments-authorize > Privacy. Flip 'Store requests' to Off. Now run a test request.
[12:31] Priya: Sending test run... request_id r_90f, stored:false, pii_redacted:["card_number"], audit_event: exported. You can see the CSV export queued.
[12:45] Ravi: I noticed the UI has a 'preview redaction' panel. Is that safe to give to devs?
[12:50] Priya: The preview shows highlighted tokens in a sandboxed view and is RBAC-protected. Devs with the proper role can use it for debugging.
[12:58] Sam: For the sample dataset, do you need full card numbers? We will provide masked tokens.
[13:03] Priya: Masked tokens are fine — for regex tuning sometimes full structured samples are needed but we can do synthetic equivalence testing.
[13:12] Maya: Let's recap and confirm next steps.
[13:16] Alex: Recap: we'll send SOC2 + KMS docs, provision a test tenant, run PII heuristic evaluation on a sample dataset, run the KV-cache benchmark, and schedule the follow-up security review.
[13:27] Maya: Sounds good. One final ask — include a note on how revoke key rotation works and its effects on stored blobs.
[13:33] Alex: We'll include that in the KO pack.
[13:35] Maya: Thanks, everyone.
[13:37] Alex: Thank you all — we'll follow up with the links and a proposed pilot timeline.
[13:41] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: Some product names and arns were abbreviated in chat; small mis-transcriptions where 'KV cache' appears as 'K-V cash' in one place; timestamps approximate.

End of transcript.
